stem: Food crops like wheat may be improved by selective breeding and genetic modification.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline how wheat crops have been improved by selective breeding.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Variation in height of a strain of wheat plants in a field shows a continuous pattern of variation.

Explain what is meant by continuous variation **and** explain why this type of variation occurs in a population.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Wheat and other crops have been genetically modified to be resistant to the herbicide glyphosate since 1996.

Fig. 4.1 shows the area of glyphosate-resistant crops grown as a percentage of the total planted hectares (plotted points) and the number of weed species with resistance to glyphosate (bars).

{{figure:figure_4_1.webp}}

Fig. 4.1

Describe and explain the relationship between the area of glyphosate-resistant crops grown and the number of resistant weed species.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Suggest **one** social advantage and **one** environmental advantage of growing glyphosate-resistant wheat.
